name: – Li Andersson – Annex I, § 1 – Am 12
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the Member States
part_text: Member States should actively promote a sustainable, social and highly competitive market economy. They should facilitate and support investment and foster innovation-led growth and productivity growth for sustainable quality job creation, notably in the context of the digital, green and demographic transitions as well as security, defence and strategic autonomy, and in light of the Union and national employment headline targets for 2030. If well anticipated and substantially funded, the transition towards sustainable, renewable and circular economies generates potential to create a significant number of new jobs and to transform existing employment into green and sustainable jobs in many sectors. Member States should pursue integrated approaches reflecting the specific challenges and development potential of the different regions and territories, including regions that are most affected by the digital, green and demographic transitions and face persistent gaps in employment opportunities, infrastructure and access to services relative to urban centres. To these ends, they should reduce unnecessary administrative burdens companies face in hiring people and scaling up, while fully respecting workers’ rights, social and environmental standards, and fostering responsible entrepreneurship and genuine self-employment. Member States should promote the development of the social economy, including social enterprises. They should develop and implement related measures and strategies, foster social innovation and encourage business models that create quality job opportunities and generate social welfare, particularly including for people that are furthest from the labour market or underrepresented.
